newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran cleric places voters after God, supreme leader.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric places voters after God, supreme leader.

text.p: A leading Iranian cleric has warned President-Elect Mohammad Khatami to put voters third, after God and supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

"The first thing is to please God...The second one is the eminent leader, the vali-e (Ayatollah Ali Khamenei). Following him are the electorate," Jannati said in a Friday sermon, broadcast by Iranian radio and monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

Jannati is a senior member of Iran's Guardian Council, a body of clerics and lawyers which has the power to reject legislation passed by the country's parliament. The council also screens candidates and oversees elections.

"All those who cast their votes have demands...Someone speaks about the inflation issue and expects inflation to be tackled, someone else speaks of administrative corruption, someone else about nepotism, another about wastage of money. Is is not easy to take up this heavy task," Jannati said.
"As for the one on whose shoulders the responsibility comes to rest, he must be most careful not to fail in this test, that he does not get low marks," he said.
Khatami, a moderate, won 69 percent of votes cast in Iran's May 23 presidential election.
